concept: The answer that cost a Kodiak hunter $150 sat on top of a stack of summaries. The camera descends through the stack to the one thick still text underneath, and the film ends by asking what you check before you hunt.
title: The Answer Was on Top

treatment.judge_reasoning: All four lenses converged on a stack of summaries. The dramatist's descent through depth gives the argument a body: bright and easy on top, dark and binding underneath, and the camera earns the trip. Grafts: the enthusiast's admiration beats (she called troopers, the trooper ran the search himself, ADF&G prints its number) and the comedian's physical spruce binder as the bottom text, which turns the abstract 'source' into an object. Comedy is confined to objects (the tag, the twin cards), never Weaver or Google's people.

angle.thesis: The answer that cost a Kodiak hunter $150 sat on top of a stack of summaries, and the one binding text, the state's regulation, is what she opened to find the right date and turn herself in.
supporting_facts: c4/c5/c8: opening the regs is how she found Oct 8 and self-reported
c6: the trooper ran the identical search and got the identical wrong answer, so the error repeats for every searcher
c13+c15: even ADF&G calls its online regs simplified, and Google's own page says check more than one place
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: Google's warning and the state's rule both existed and she still paid $150; but a wrong answer that replicates for every searcher (c6) and that DPS expects to see again (c9,c11) is not one hunter's slip. Nothing in the file says what the AI cited, so no claim about Google's sourcing.
angle.falsifiability: False if the trooper's identical search had returned a correct date, or if ADF&G's own published listing said Sept 1 (the booklet did not load, so this is disclosed as unverified).
angle.second_movement: c13 recontextualizes the 'one source of truth' line: it is itself a simplified convenience over the statute, so the honest lesson is a stack of summaries over one binding text, not AI bad and the official page good.
angle.valence: mixed, respectful of Weaver, constructive, no scold, no pile-on at Google
runner_ups: Honesty as the working safeguard (self-report + replication)
Provenance ask: AI answers that name the ADF&G source (booklet did not load so the falsifier is open)
angle.why_runner_ups_lost: each is a sub-beat of the chosen thesis; the provenance ask overreaches the evidence (nothing says what the AI cited)

hook.pattern_note: an ordinary search plus an object that doesn't belong in the frame: a closed binder. The question it raises is what is in the binder.

open_loop.what: a thick spruce binder sits closed by the phone on the kitchen table and its page is never shown. The film refuses to open it until the hands peel the summaries away and the page reads GENERAL SEASON: OCT 8.

open_loop_2.what: Weren't there warnings? There were, and the film concedes them at full weight, then withholds the catch in the state's own source until the envelope's fine print types on.

divergence_note: Against 2026-09-23 (frontal document, split-compare, divide-and-settle, document-as-subject, dusk violet and copper) and 2026-09-19 (macro-closeup, single-object-void, radial-emanate, structure-as-subject, powerhouse green and amber) this film is a vertical CROSS-SECTION DESCENT through a stack in STACKED-LAYERS with a VERTICAL-DESCENT motion vector, a triple none of the last four films used. Its register is tactile collage, its camera strategy dolly-through, its light overcast-diffuse. Its palette shares no colour role with either: fog green, hunter orange, spruce, cream.
